verification_policy: Every document verified against official .gov.in domain or authoritative legal database. No synthetic content. URLs fetched or search-confirmed. Content limited to information explicitly supported by source.

documents.title: Mahabhulekh Portal - 7/12 Extract Online Viewing Service
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: 7/12 Extract (Satbara Utara) viewing and download
documents.content: The Mahabhulekh portal (bhulekh.mahabhumi.gov.in) is the official Maharashtra government portal for viewing land records. Citizens can view 7/12 extracts (Satbara Utara) by selecting district, taluka, and village, then entering the survey number. The portal displays current ownership details, land area, crop details, and mutation entries. The extract shows the Record of Rights (RoR) information maintained by the Revenue Department. The portal is maintained by the Maharashtra Land Records Department and provides free viewing of unsigned 7/12 extracts. For legally valid digitally signed extracts, citizens are directed to the Digital Satbara portal (digitalsatbara.mahabhumi.gov.in). The portal covers all districts of Maharashtra and is integrated with the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP).

documents.title: Digital Satbara Portal - Digitally Signed 7/12 Extract
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Digitally signed 7/12 extract with legal validity
documents.content: The Digital Satbara portal (digitalsatbara.mahabhumi.gov.in) provides legally valid, digitally signed 7/12 extracts (Satbara Utara) for Maharashtra. Unlike the unsigned extracts on Mahabhulekh, these digitally signed documents carry legal validity for official purposes. Citizens can obtain digitally signed 7/12, 8A extracts, and Property Cards through this portal. The digital signature ensures authenticity and non-repudiation. The portal requires user registration and payment of prescribed fees. The digitally signed extracts are generated from the official land records database maintained by the Revenue Department. This service is part of Maharashtra's DILRMP implementation and e-governance initiatives for transparent land administration.

documents.title: Aapli Chawadi (e-Chawadi) Portal - Mutation Notice and Objection
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Mutation notice publication, objection submission, and status tracking
documents.content: The Aapli Chawadi (e-Chawadi) portal (echawadicitizen.mahabhumi.gov.in) is the official Maharashtra government platform for mutation (ferfar) notice management. Under the eMutation workflow of DILRMP/NLRMP, when a property registration occurs, the registration details are automatically transferred to the mutation cell at the Tehsil office. Digitally signed mutation notices are generated and sent back to the originating Sub-Registrar Office (SRO). The SRO serves the notices and returns them to the Tehsil Office and Village Accountant with registration details. The mutation process is initiated instantly upon registration. After completion of the notice period, the mutation entry is certified by the Circle Officer and the Record of Rights (RoR) is updated. The portal allows citizens to view mutation notices, submit objections, and track mutation status online. All types of registered and non-registered documents are covered under this system.

documents.title: eFerfar Portal - Online Mutation Application and Tracking
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Online mutation (ferfar) application, tracking, and workflow
documents.content: The eFerfar portal (mahaferfar.enlightcloud.com) is the official Maharashtra government portal for online mutation (ferfar) services. Citizens can apply for mutation entries, track application status, and view mutation records through this portal. The portal is integrated with the eMutation workflow under the National Land Records Modernization Programme (NLRMP). The workflow involves: (1) Registration details captured from the Registration Office and transferred to the Mutation Cell at Tehsil office; (2) Digitally signed notices generated and sent to originating SRO; (3) SRO serves notices and returns to Tehsil Office with registration details; (4) Mutation entry certified by Circle Officer after notice period completion; (5) Record of Rights updated. The portal provides end-to-end digitization of the mutation process, reducing citizen interface with government offices.

documents.title: Inspector General of Registration (IGR) Maharashtra Official Portal
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Property registration, stamp duty, e-Search, and citizen services
documents.content: The IGR Maharashtra portal (igrmaharashtra.gov.in) is the official portal of the Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra. Key services include: (1) Ready Reckoner Rate search - government minimum property values by zone and property type used for stamp duty calculation; (2) Market Value Search / Property Valuation - calculate approximate stamp duty based on property details; (3) Index-II / Encumbrance Certificate - history of registered transactions against a property for title verification; (4) e-Stamp Verification - verify authenticity of electronic stamp papers; (5) Document Search - search previously registered documents by survey number, plot number, or party name; (6) Appointment Booking - book registration appointments at Sub-Registrar Offices; (7) Marriage Registration - online registration and certificate services. For Mumbai, a dedicated sub-portal (igrmaharashtra.gov.in/eASR) provides Annual Statement of Rates. The portal supports online payment of stamp duty and registration fees through e-SBTR or GRAS.

documents.title: IGR Maharashtra Free e-Search Service
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Free online search of registered property documents and transactions
documents.content: The IGR Maharashtra Free e-Search service (freesearchigrservice.maharashtra.gov.in) allows citizens to search registered property documents online without charge. Users can search by: District, Taluka, Village; Survey Number, Plot Number, CTS Number; or Party Name. The search displays registered transactions including sale deeds, mortgages, releases, and other encumbrances. Mumbai City and Suburban records are searchable from 1985; most other districts from 2002. The e-Search provides preliminary information and is not a legally certified document. For legal purposes, citizens must obtain a certified copy or Index-II from the Sub-Registrar Office. The service is intended for due diligence before property transactions. Users should search for a minimum of 13 years (preferably 30 years) to ensure comprehensive title verification. The portal lists every registered document hit and allows downloading of search results.

documents.title: IGR Maharashtra Paid Document Search and Certified Copy Service
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Paid search for registered documents and certified copy issuance
documents.content: The IGR Maharashtra portal provides paid document search and certified copy services. Citizens can obtain certified copies of registered documents (Index-II) by applying online or visiting the Sub-Registrar Office. The process involves: selecting district and Sub-Registrar Office; entering property details (survey number, CTS number, plot number) or document number; specifying the search period; paying applicable fees online (net banking, debit/credit card, UPI); and downloading the certified document. For digitized records, documents are available for instant download as digitally signed PDFs. For non-digitized records, processing takes 3-5 working days. Fees vary based on search duration and document type. The certified copies carry legal validity and are required for property transactions, loan applications, and legal proceedings. The portal also provides e-Stamp verification services to confirm authenticity of electronic stamp papers.

documents.title: Maharashtra Registration Rules, 1961
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Registration procedure, office hours, document handling, fees, indexes
documents.content: The Maharashtra Registration Rules, 1961, made under Section 69 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, govern property registration procedures in Maharashtra. Key provisions: Office hours - Registration offices open daily (except Sundays, second and fourth Saturdays, and holidays) from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in Bombay/Bombay Suburban districts, and 10:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. elsewhere with 30-minute recess. Documents must be presented at least one hour before closing time. In grave emergencies, documents may be accepted at private residences with immediate reporting to the Registrar. Register books - Five register books (Forms A-E) maintained under Section 50. Additional register books opened when necessary. Day Book (Form G) and Cash Book (Form H) maintained daily. Indexes - Prepared in Marathi (Forms M, N, O, P). European/American names indexed alphabetically under surname; Indian names under personal name. Fines for delayed registration: delay up to 1 month - up to 2.5x registration fee; 1-2 months - up to 5x; 2-3 months - up to 7.5x; 3-4 months - up to 10x. Documents impounded for insufficient stamp duty shall not be copied or certified until returned with Collector's certificate. Monthly work statements submitted by Sub-Registrars to Registrars, and by Registrars to Inspector General by the 5th of each month.

documents.title: Maharashtra Land Revenue (Appeals, Revision and Review) Rules, 1967
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Appeals, revision, and review procedures under Maharashtra Land Revenue Code
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue (Appeals, Revision and Review) Rules, 1967, made under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966, prescribe the procedure for filing appeals, revisions, and reviews against revenue officer decisions. Appeals under Section 257 of the MLRC can be filed against orders of Tahsildars and other revenue officers. The rules specify: (1) Form and content of appeal memoranda; (2) Time limits for filing appeals (typically 60 days from date of order, with provision for condonation of delay); (3) Fees for filing appeals; (4) Procedure for stay of execution pending appeal; (5) Powers of appellate authorities (Sub-Divisional Officer, Collector, Commissioner); (6) Revision jurisdiction of Collector and Commissioner under Section 258; (7) Review powers under Section 259. The appellate authority may confirm, modify, or set aside the original order. The rules ensure due process in revenue disputes and provide a hierarchical mechanism for grievance redressal. All appeals must be filed in the prescribed format with necessary documents and court fees.

documents.title: Maharashtra Land Revenue (Boundaries and Boundary Marks) Rules, 1969
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Boundary marks, survey marks, demarcation, and maintenance procedures
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue (Boundaries and Boundary Marks) Rules, 1969, prescribe standards for boundary and survey marks. Authorized boundary marks include: (A) Continuous marks - boundary strips (0.46m wide, 0.61m high in dry crop lands; 0.23m wide, 0.61m high in rice/garden lands), dhuras/sarbandhas (1.22m wide, 0.61m high), hedges; (B) Discontinuous marks - dressed long stones, masonry pillars, earthen mounds/cairns. Maintenance responsibility lies with the holder of the survey number with the lowest number on a common boundary, unless the Collector orders otherwise. Quinquennial repair programme fixed by Collector. General notice given by Tahsildar by 1st November; holders must complete repairs by 30th November. Circle Inspector inspects between 1-31 December; Talathi issues individual notices in Form C requiring repairs within one month. If not repaired, government carries out repairs at holder's cost. Demarcation on application: holder applies to Collector with prescribed fees; Collector causes measurement by District Inspector and fixes boundary marks. Cost of materials and labour paid by holder. Single boundary mark system may be introduced if half the holders desire it. Plan for straightening crooked boundaries published in village with 15-day objection period. Village committee constituted to determine compensation for boundary revision.

documents.title: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958
documents.department: Finance Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Stamp duty on instruments including property conveyance, mortgage, and lease
documents.content: The Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958 (formerly Bombay Stamp Act) governs stamp duty on instruments in Maharashtra. Key provisions: Section 3 - charge of stamp duty on instruments; Section 4 - rates of duty specified in Schedule I; Section 33 - power of Collector to determine duty on instruments not duly stamped; Section 35 - penalty for non-payment or short payment; Section 40 - recovery of deficit stamp duty. For property transactions: Conveyance deed - stamp duty based on market value or consideration, whichever is higher; Mortgage deed - specific rates based on amount secured; Lease deed - rates based on lease period and rent. The Act provides for: (1) Adjudication of stamp duty by Collector; (2) Refund of excess stamp duty under Section 47; (3) Penalties for evasion; (4) Compounding of offences. E-stamping facility available through SHCIL (Stock Holding Corporation of India Limited). The Ready Reckoner/Annual Statement of Rates (ASR) published by IGR Maharashtra determines market value for stamp duty calculation. Stamp duty must be paid before or at the time of registration. Documents not duly stamped are impounded by the registering officer and forwarded to the Collector for determination of proper duty.

documents.title: Aaple Sarkar Portal - Revenue Department Online Services
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Online revenue services including land records, mutation, and certificates
documents.content: The Aaple Sarkar portal (aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in) provides online access to Revenue Department services in Maharashtra. Key land-record and property-related services include: (1) Certified copy of 7/12 extract - time limit 7 days; (2) Certified copy of 8A extract - time limit 7 days; (3) Certified copy of Property Card - time limit 7 days; (4) Land Measurement - time limit 30 days; (5) Mutation/Change in Records (Ferfar) - time limit 30 days; (6) Subdivision of Land (Hissa) - time limit 30 days; (7) Correction in Land Records - time limit 30 days; (8) Non-Agricultural (NA) Permission services. Citizens can apply online, upload documents, pay fees, and track application status. The portal integrates with Mahabhulekh, Digital Satbara, and other land record systems. Services are delivered under the Right to Public Services Act with prescribed time limits. The portal also provides grievance redressal mechanism for delayed services. Required documents typically include identity proof, ownership documents, survey numbers, and applicable fees.

documents.title: MAITRI Portal - Maharashtra Industry, Trade and Investment Facilitation Portal
documents.department: Industries Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Single window clearance for industrial land, NA permission, and business approvals
documents.content: The MAITRI portal (maitri.maharashtra.gov.in) is the official Maharashtra government single-window facilitation system for industry, trade, and investment. It integrates land-related approvals including Non-Agricultural (NA) permission, land allotment, and building plan approvals. The portal provides: (1) Online application for industrial land allotment; (2) NA conversion tracking; (3) Building permission management system (BPMS) / Auto DCR integration; (4) Payment of one-time conversion premium through GRAS; (5) Status tracking of approvals. Under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code (Second Amendment) Act, 2025, NA conversion is integrated with planning permissions through MAITRI/BPMS. For lands where NA use is permitted under development plans, separate Collector permission is not required; planning authority grants development permission directly. One-time premium replaces recurring NA assessments. The portal aims to reduce approval timelines to 15-30 days and eliminate administrative duplication between revenue and planning authorities.

documents.title: Dharashiv District eMutation Implementation under NLRMP
documents.department: Revenue Department, Dharashiv District, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: eMutation workflow, notice generation, and Record of Rights update
documents.content: The Dharashiv District official page documents the eMutation implementation under the National Land Records Modernization Programme (NLRMP). The entire mutation workflow is computerized: (1) Information from the Registration Office is captured and transferred to the Mutation Cell at Tehsil office; (2) Digitally signed mutation notices are generated and sent to the originating SRO office; (3) The SRO office serves the notices and sends them back to Tehsil Office and Village Accountant with registration details; (4) The mutation process is initiated instantly upon registration; (5) The mutation entry is certified by the Circle Officer after completion of the notice period; (6) The Record of Rights (RoR) is updated. This system covers all types of registered and non-registered documents. Key portal links: eFerfar Website (mahaferfar.enlightcloud.com); View 7/12 (bhulekh.mahabhumi.gov.in); Digitally signed 7/12 (aapleabhilekh.mahabhumi.gov.in/Satbara). The system relieves citizens from waiting for manual notice service by Talathi and enables online application and tracking.

documents.title: Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 - Mutation Provisions (Sections 149-157)
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Legal provisions for mutation of land records after transfer, inheritance, and other events
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 contains key provisions governing mutation (ferfar) of land records. Section 149 - Power to enter names of landowners in record of rights; Section 150 - Power to enter names of tenants and other occupants; Section 154 - Procedure for mutation on transfer of land including sale, gift, mortgage, lease, or inheritance; Section 157 - Power of revenue officers to correct entries in record of rights. The Code mandates that mutations be carried out by authorized revenue officers (Tahsildar, Circle Officer) after due enquiry. For mutations based on registered documents, the process is initiated automatically upon registration. For non-registered transfers (inheritance, court orders), applications must be submitted with supporting documents. The Code provides for: (1) Public notice of proposed mutations; (2) Period for objections (typically 15-30 days); (3) Enquiry into objections by revenue officer; (4) Approval or rejection of mutation with reasons; (5) Appeal against mutation orders under Section 257. The Record of Rights must be updated to reflect mutations for the land revenue system to function accurately.

documents.title: Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 - NA Conversion Provisions (Sections 42, 44, 47A)
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Non-agricultural land use conversion, permission, and premium
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 governs conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural (NA) use. Section 42 - Power to grant permission for use of land for non-agricultural purposes; Section 44 - Restriction on use of land for non-agricultural purposes without permission; Section 47A - Levy of non-agricultural assessment. Under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code (Second Amendment) Act, 2025: (1) No separate Collector permission is required for NA conversion if the proposed use is permissible under draft/final development plan or regional plan; (2) Planning authority (municipal corporation/council/special planning authority) grants development permission directly under MRTP Act; (3) One-time conversion premium replaces recurring NA assessments, calculated as percentage of market value per Annual Statement of Rates: up to 1,000 sqm - 0.1%; 1,000-4,000 sqm - 0.25%; above 4,000 sqm - 0.5%; (4) Premium paid through GRAS portal; (5) Revenue records updated automatically through BPMS/Auto DCR after development permission. For lands not covered by development plans or Class-II lands, Collector permission still required with applicable grant/premium.

documents.title: Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 - Appeal, Revision, and Review Provisions (Sections 257-259)
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Appeal, revision, and review against revenue officer decisions
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 provides a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism. Section 257 - Appeals: Any person aggrieved by an order of a Tahsildar or other revenue officer may appeal to the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) within 60 days. Appeals from SDO orders lie to the Collector. Appeals from Collector orders lie to the Commissioner (Divisional level). Appeals from Assistant Superintendent of Land Records lie to the District Superintendent. Section 258 - Revision: The Collector and Commissioner have revision powers over orders of subordinate revenue officers. Revision can be initiated suo moto or on application. The revisional authority may call for records, examine legality and propriety of orders, and pass appropriate orders. Section 259 - Review: Power of revenue officers to review their own orders in certain circumstances. The revenue hierarchy is: Village Level (Talathi/Patwari) -> Circle Level (Circle Officer/Inspector) -> Taluka Level (Tahsildar) -> Sub-Division Level (SDO) -> District Level (Collector) -> Divisional Level (Commissioner) -> State Level (Secretary, Revenue Department). Time limits for appeals are strictly enforced, with provision for condonation of delay on sufficient cause being shown.

documents.title: IGR Maharashtra Ready Reckoner and Annual Statement of Rates (ASR)
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Government minimum property valuation for stamp duty and registration fee calculation
documents.content: The Ready Reckoner (Annual Statement of Rates) published by IGR Maharashtra determines the minimum market value of properties for stamp duty and registration fee calculation. The rates are revised annually, effective 1st January each year. Citizens can search rates on igrmaharashtra.gov.in by: selecting financial year; selecting District, Taluka, and Village/City area; selecting property type (residential flat, open land, office, shop, industrial, agricultural). The applicable rate per square metre or square foot is displayed. For Mumbai, a dedicated sub-portal (igrmaharashtra.gov.in/eASR) provides Annual Statement of Rates. The Ready Reckoner rate is the minimum value for stamp duty calculation; if the actual transaction value is higher, duty is levied on the higher amount. The rates are used for: (1) Stamp duty on conveyance deeds; (2) Registration fees; (3) Court fee calculations; (4) NA conversion premium calculations (as percentage of market value per ASR); (5) Property tax assessments. The rates are determined based on location, infrastructure, and market conditions.

documents.title: IGR Maharashtra e-Stamp and e-SBTR Payment Services
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Electronic stamp duty payment and verification
documents.content: The IGR Maharashtra portal provides electronic stamp duty payment facilities through e-Stamp and e-SBTR (Stamp Duty and Registration). Citizens can: (1) Purchase e-Stamp certificates through authorized vendors; (2) Pay stamp duty online through the GRAS (Government Receipt Accounting System) portal; (3) Verify e-Stamp authenticity by entering the Certificate Number on the IGR portal. The e-Stamp verification system confirms whether the e-stamp is genuine, the party it was issued to, and the stamp duty value. The portal supports online payment of stamp duty and registration fees through net banking, debit/credit cards, and UPI. For property registration, stamp duty must be paid before or at the time of document presentation at the Sub-Registrar Office. The e-SBTR system generates a unique reference number for each payment, which must be quoted during registration. Refund of excess stamp duty can be claimed under Section 47 of the Maharashtra Stamp Act with application to the Collector.

documents.title: Aaple Sarkar - Land Measurement Application Service
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Application for land measurement, survey, and demarcation
documents.content: The Aaple Sarkar portal provides online application for land measurement services with a prescribed time limit of 30 days. The process involves: (1) Citizen applies online or at Taluka office; (2) Application submitted to concerned authority (Tahsildar); (3) Tahsildar examines application and, if satisfied, passes orders to Revenue Inspector or District Inspector of Land Records for demarcation; (4) Measurement work completed within specified timeframe; (5) Revenue Inspector prepares spot memo at time of demarcation, signed by all parties and witnesses; (6) Demarcation report submitted to Tahsildar. Under the 2025 reform, licensed private surveyors can now conduct official land measurements with same legal validity as government surveyors, reducing timelines to 30 days. Fees are prescribed by the Commissioner and Director, Land Records, Pune (Order No. LR/227/CR/3926/Land-3/2001, dated 30th October 2001). For disputed boundaries, the Collector may order demarcation under the Maharashtra Land Revenue (Boundaries and Boundary Marks) Rules, 1969. Measurement reports are incorporated into land records for boundary verification.

documents.title: Aaple Sarkar - Mutation (Ferfar) Application Service
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Online application for mutation of land records after sale, inheritance, gift, or court order
documents.content: The Aaple Sarkar portal provides online mutation (ferfar) application services with a prescribed time limit of 30 days. Types of mutations covered: (1) Mutation after sale/registration - automatic under eMutation; (2) Mutation after inheritance/death - requires death certificate, legal heir certificate, and application; (3) Mutation after gift - requires registered gift deed; (4) Mutation after partition - requires partition deed; (5) Mutation after court order - requires certified court order. The process: (1) Citizen applies online with required documents; (2) Application forwarded to Taluka mutation cell; (3) Verification and enquiry by Circle Officer/Revenue Inspector; (4) Public notice issued via e-Chawadi for objection period; (5) If no objections, mutation approved and Record of Rights updated; (6) If objections, hearing conducted and decision passed. Required documents vary by mutation type but typically include: identity proof, ownership documents (sale deed, inheritance documents), death certificate (for inheritance), survey number details, and applicable fees. The portal allows status tracking and provides digitally signed mutation entries.

documents.title: Aaple Sarkar - Land Subdivision (Hissa) Application Service
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Application for subdivision of land parcel and creation of new survey numbers
documents.content: The Aaple Sarkar portal provides online land subdivision (hissa) application services with a prescribed time limit of 30 days. The process involves: (1) Citizen applies online or at Taluka office with required documents; (2) Application submitted to Tahsildar for verification; (3) Land measurement conducted by Revenue Inspector or licensed surveyor to demarcate new boundaries; (4) Subdivision plan prepared and published in village for objections; (5) If no objections, subdivision approved and new survey numbers (hissa numbers) assigned; (6) Record of Rights updated to reflect new parcels. Required documents include: application form, 7/12 extract showing current ownership, partition deed or family settlement (if applicable), survey plan, identity proof, and applicable fees. The subdivision creates new gat/hissa numbers within the original survey number. Each new parcel gets separate entries in land records. The process is governed by the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code and requires approval from the Tahsildar or higher authority depending on parcel size and location.

documents.title: Aaple Sarkar - Land Record Correction Application Service
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Application for correction of errors in land records including name, area, and survey number
documents.content: The Aaple Sarkar portal provides online land record correction services with a prescribed time limit of 30 days. Types of corrections covered: (1) Name correction - spelling errors, name changes; (2) Area correction - discrepancies in recorded land area; (3) Survey/Gat number correction - errors in survey number entries; (4) Boundary correction - errors in boundary descriptions; (5) Classification correction - errors in land use classification. The process: (1) Citizen applies online with supporting documents; (2) Application verified by Talathi/Circle Officer; (3) Field inspection conducted if required; (4) Correction approved by Tahsildar or higher authority; (5) Record of Rights updated. Required documents include: application form, proof of correct information (Aadhaar, PAN, passport for name correction; measurement report for area correction; old and new survey maps for survey number correction), 7/12 extract, and applicable fees. If correction is rejected, applicant may appeal to the Sub-Divisional Officer under Section 257 of the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code. Corrections are reflected in updated 7/12 and 8A extracts.

documents.title: Aaple Sarkar - Property Card Extract and Correction Services
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Property Card extract viewing, certified copies, and corrections for urban land records
documents.content: The Aaple Sarkar portal provides Property Card services for urban land records in Maharashtra. Services include: (1) Certified copy of Property Card - time limit 7 days; (2) Property Card correction - time limit 30 days. The Property Card is the urban equivalent of the 7/12 extract and contains: property description, owner details, area, building details, assessment details, and mutation entries. For urban properties (especially in Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur), the Property Card is maintained by the City Survey Department. Citizens can view Property Cards online through Mahabhulekh (bhulekh.mahabhumi.gov.in) and obtain certified copies through Digital Satbara or Aaple Sarkar. Property Card mutation follows a similar process to rural mutation but is handled by the municipal corporation or City Survey Office. Required documents for certified copy: application form, property details (CTS number, plot number, building name), identity proof, and fees. For corrections: supporting documents proving correct information, existing Property Card copy, and applicable fees. The Property Card is essential for property transactions, loan applications, and legal proceedings in urban areas.

documents.title: IGR Maharashtra - Registration Fees and Document Handling Charges
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Schedule of registration fees, document handling charges, and fines for delayed registration
documents.content: The IGR Maharashtra prescribes registration fees and document handling charges under the Indian Registration Act, 1908 and Maharashtra Registration Rules, 1961. Registration fees: Conveyance deed - 1% of market value or consideration (subject to minimum and maximum limits); Mortgage deed - specific percentage of amount secured; Lease deed - based on period and premium; Gift deed - 1% of market value; Partition deed - 1% of value of separated share. Document handling charges: scanning, digitization, and preservation charges per document. Fines for delayed registration (Section 25): delay up to 1 month - up to 2.5x registration fee; 1-2 months - up to 5x; 2-3 months - up to 7.5x; 3-4 months - up to 10x. The Registrar has discretion to impose smaller fines in suitable cases. Stamp duty rates (under Maharashtra Stamp Act): Conveyance - 5% (urban) / 3% (rural) of market value or consideration, whichever is higher; Registration fee - 1% of market value. Total registration cost typically includes: stamp duty + registration fee + document handling charges + scanning charges. Women purchasers may get concession in stamp duty in certain areas. Fees are payable through GRAS portal, e-SBTR, or authorized banks.

documents.title: Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) Guidelines, Technical Manuals and MIS 2021-2026
documents.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
documents.topic: DILRMP implementation guidelines for digitization of land records, registration, and revenue courts
documents.content: The DILRMP Guidelines 2021-2026 provide the operational framework for the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme. Key components: (1) Computerization of land records - textual records digitization, Record of Rights (RoR) updating, integration with registration; (2) Survey/re-survey - cadastral mapping, geo-referencing, ULPIN generation; (3) Computerization of Registration - NGDRS implementation, e-Registration, integration with land records; (4) Revenue Court integration - computerization of revenue courts and linking with land records; (5) Modern Record Rooms - digitization of old records; (6) Training and capacity building. The guidelines specify funding pattern (100% central sector scheme), implementation through state/UT governments with district as unit of implementation. Technical manuals cover: cadastral map digitization standards, data migration protocols, software specifications, security requirements. The programme aims for: updated land records, automatic mutation, integration of textual and spatial records, inter-connectivity between revenue and registration, and transition to conclusive titling. ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar) is a 14-digit unique identifier for each land parcel based on geo-coordinates.

documents.title: DILRMP 3.0 Operational Guidelines 2026-2031
documents.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
documents.topic: Next phase of DILRMP with enhanced integration and conclusive titling
documents.content: DILRMP 3.0 represents the next phase of the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme for 2026-2031. Building on DILRMP 2.0, the new phase focuses on: (1) Conclusive titling with title guarantee - moving from presumptive to conclusive title system; (2) Enhanced integration - linking land records with Aadhaar (consent-based), revenue courts, banks, and other stakeholders; (3) Real-time mutation - automatic mutation triggered by registration with minimal human intervention; (4) Citizen-centric services - single-window access to all land-related services; (5) Data analytics and land banks - using digitized land data for planning and development; (6) Blockchain and emerging technologies - exploring distributed ledger technology for tamper-proof records. The programme continues as a 100% centrally funded scheme. States are required to: complete cadastral map digitization, achieve 100% ULPIN coverage, integrate registration with land records, computerize all revenue courts, and establish modern record rooms. The guidelines emphasize data security, privacy protection, and interoperability standards across states.

documents.title: National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS) Official Portal
documents.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
documents.topic: Generic configurable software for property registration across Indian states
documents.content: The National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS) is a common, generic, and configurable application developed by the Department of Land Resources for registration departments across India. NGDRS facilitates states to create state-specific instances and configure the software as per local requirements. Key features: (1) Citizen interface for online document entry, property valuation, and stamp duty calculation; (2) Sub-Registrar interface for document verification, biometric authentication, and registration; (3) Restriction on transactions of prohibited properties (government land, tribal land, mortgaged land); (4) Online appointment booking; (5) e-Stamp integration; (6) Grievance redressal mechanism. States using NGDRS include: Maharashtra (CIDCO, Pvt. Builder Module, e-Registration, e-Filing 2.0), Chhattisgarh, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Manipur, Mizoram, Punjab, Tripura, Delhi (DORIS 2.2), Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Andaman & Nicobar. Citizens can: calculate circle rates, compute stamp duty, submit documents online, make instant payments, and book appointments. Physical visit to Sub-Registrar office is required only once for final signing and biometric verification.

documents.title: Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) / Bhu-Aadhaar Technical Framework
documents.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
documents.topic: 14-digit unique land parcel identification based on geo-coordinates
documents.content: The Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) or Bhu-Aadhaar is a 14-digit alpha-numeric unique ID assigned to each land parcel in India. Developed by NIC under DILRMP, the ULPIN is generated based on the longitude and latitude coordinates of the land parcel using geo-referenced cadastral maps. The 14-digit structure contains: State code, District code, Sub-district code, Village code, and Unique plot ID. ULPIN follows Electronic Commerce Code Manufacturers Association (ECCMA) guidelines and international standards. Key features: (1) Permanent attachment to geographic boundary - remains same even if land is transferred, subdivided, or undergoes changes; (2) Stamped on physical land record documents held by owners; (3) Enables unique identification and retrieval of records; (4) Facilitates integration of land records with registration, revenue courts, and banks; (5) Supports conclusive titling. As of 2023, ULPIN rolled out in 26 States/UTs including Maharashtra. Andhra Pradesh achieved 100% coverage first. Geo-referencing is a pre-condition for ULPIN generation. The BhuNaksha software uses georeferenced revenue village shape files to generate ULPIN.

documents.title: Draft Registration Bill, 2025 - Public Consultation
documents.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
documents.topic: Proposed new registration legislation to replace Indian Registration Act, 1908
documents.content: The Department of Land Resources invited public suggestions on the draft Registration Bill, 2025, which proposes to replace the Indian Registration Act, 1908. The Bill aims to modernize property registration laws to align with digital governance and current property transaction needs. Key proposed features: (1) Mandatory electronic registration and e-filing; (2) Integration with land records and ULPIN; (3) Real-time updating of encumbrance records; (4) Enhanced penalties for registration fraud; (5) Streamlined procedures for document registration; (6) Provision for conclusive titling framework; (7) Standardized registration processes across states. The draft was published for public consultation with a 30-day comment period. Stakeholders including state governments, legal experts, and citizens were invited to provide feedback. The Bill represents a significant reform in property registration law, intended to reduce disputes, improve transparency, and facilitate ease of doing business in real estate transactions.

documents.title: Department of Land Resources - Acts, Rules, Policies, and Programmes
documents.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
documents.topic: Central government land resources policies including DILRMP, watershed development, and land reforms
documents.content: The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, oversees national land administration policies. Key programmes: (1) Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) - digitization of land records, registration, and revenue courts; (2) Watershed Development Component-Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 2.0 - watershed management and land conservation; (3) Institutional Research Grant for Land Administration. The portal provides access to: Acts and Rules (including draft Registration Bill 2025), DILRMP guidelines and technical manuals, programme implementation documents, e-Auction notices for office equipment, and stakeholder consultation documents. DoLR coordinates with state/UT governments for implementation of centrally sponsored and central sector schemes. The department is headed by the Minister of Rural Development. Current focus areas include: conclusive titling, ULPIN implementation, NGDRS rollout, revenue court computerization, and integration of land records with other government databases.

documents.title: IGR Maharashtra e-Registration and e-Filing Services
documents.department: Inspector General of Registration, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Online property document filing, appointment booking, and pre-registration data entry
documents.content: The IGR Maharashtra e-Registration and e-Filing services enable citizens to complete pre-registration formalities online. The process: (1) Citizen registers on the IGR portal; (2) Enters property details, party details, and transaction type; (3) System calculates stamp duty and registration fees based on Ready Reckoner rates; (4) Citizen pays stamp duty through e-SBTR or GRAS; (5) Uploads scanned documents; (6) Books appointment at Sub-Registrar Office; (7) Visits SRO on scheduled date with original documents and parties for biometric verification and final registration; (8) Receives digitally signed registration deed and Index-II. The e-Filing 2.0 system (part of NGDRS) allows: online document entry by citizens, automatic property valuation, stamp duty calculation, e-Stamp verification, and appointment management. For Maharashtra, NGDRS modules include: CIDCO module, Private Builder Module, and e-Filing 2.0. The system restricts transactions on prohibited properties (government land, tribal land, mortgaged land). Post-registration, the system automatically triggers mutation workflow in revenue records through DILRMP integration.

documents.title: Maharashtra Revenue Authority Hierarchy and Jurisdiction
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Hierarchy of revenue officers from village to state level with defined powers and jurisdiction
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 establishes the revenue authority hierarchy: (1) Village Level - Talathi/Patwari (maintains village accounts, Record of Rights, assists in revenue collection); (2) Circle Level - Circle Officer/Inspector (supervises 8-10 villages, verifies mutations, conducts inspections); (3) Taluka Level - Tahsildar (executive magistrate, approves mutations, conducts enquiries, issues certificates); (4) Sub-Division Level - Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) - hears appeals against Tahsildar orders, supervises talukas; (5) District Level - Collector (district revenue head, hears appeals from SDO, revision jurisdiction, land acquisition, NA permission in certain cases); (6) Divisional Level - Commissioner (hears appeals from Collector, revision jurisdiction over district officers); (7) State Level - Secretary, Revenue Department (policy and appellate authority). Additional officers: District Superintendent of Land Records (technical head for survey and measurement), Assistant Superintendent of Land Records (taluka-level survey supervision), District Inspector of Land Records (conducts measurements and demarcation). The hierarchy ensures systematic grievance redressal with defined appeal pathways under Sections 257-259 of MLRC.

documents.title: Mahabhulekh and Digital Satbara - 8A Extract (Land Account) Services
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: 8A extract viewing, download, and certified copy services
documents.content: The 8A extract (Village Form 8A) is the land account record showing: holder's name, survey number, area, assessment, land revenue, and other charges. It complements the 7/12 extract by providing financial and assessment details. Citizens can view 8A extracts free on Mahabhulekh (bhulekh.mahabhumi.gov.in) by selecting district, taluka, village, and survey number. For legally valid certified copies, citizens use Digital Satbara (digitalsatbara.mahabhumi.gov.in) or Aaple Sarkar. The 8A extract shows: (1) Land revenue assessment; (2) Non-agricultural assessment (if applicable); (3) Outstanding dues; (4) Payment history; (5) Land classification. Corrections in 8A require application to the Tahsildar with supporting documents. The extract is essential for: property transactions, loan applications, NA conversion applications, and revenue dispute resolution. The 8A is maintained by the Talathi at village level and updated by the Circle Officer/Tahsildar. Digitally signed 8A extracts carry legal validity and are accepted by courts, banks, and government offices.

documents.title: Maharashtra Property Card - Urban Land Records System
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Urban land records maintenance through Property Card system
documents.content: The Property Card is the urban equivalent of the 7/12 extract for city-surveyed areas in Maharashtra. It is maintained by the City Survey Department and contains: property description (CTS number, plot number, building name), owner details, area measurements, building details, assessment information, and mutation entries. Property Cards are available for viewing on Mahabhulekh and as certified copies through Digital Satbara or Aaple Sarkar. The Property Card mutation process: (1) Application submitted with sale deed/transfer document; (2) Verification by City Survey Office; (3) Notice issued for objections; (4) Mutation approved after objection period; (5) Property Card updated. Required documents: registered sale deed, previous Property Card, identity proof, NOC from society (for flats), and applicable fees. The Property Card is essential for: property transactions in urban areas, mortgage/loan applications, property tax assessments, and legal proceedings. In Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur, and other municipal areas, the Property Card replaces the 7/12 extract as the primary land record document.

documents.title: Maharashtra Land Record Correction Procedures under MLRC
documents.department: Revenue and Forest Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.topic: Procedures for correcting errors in land records including name, area, survey number
documents.content: The Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 provides procedures for correction of errors in land records under Section 157 and related provisions. Types of corrections: (1) Clerical errors - spelling mistakes, transcription errors (corrected by Tahsildar on application); (2) Substantive errors - incorrect area, wrong survey number, incorrect boundary (requires enquiry and field verification); (3) Name corrections - due to marriage, legal name change, or spelling errors (requires documentary proof). Process: (1) Application to Tahsildar with supporting documents; (2) Verification by Talathi/Circle Officer; (3) Field inspection if required; (4) Notice to affected parties if substantive change; (5) Order passed by Tahsildar or higher authority; (6) Record of Rights updated. For errors arising from survey: application to District Superintendent of Land Records for re-survey and correction. Appeals against correction orders lie to the Sub-Divisional Officer under Section 257. Time limit for correction applications: no statutory limit, but delay may require explanation. Required documents: application, proof of correct information, existing 7/12/Property Card, identity proof, and court fees. Corrections are reflected in subsequent extracts issued from the updated records.
